issue:434.title: Let a theme provide how a pane looks, with a sun and moon in the scrapbook pane
issue:434.author: neoworks-bot
issue:434.body:
Today how a pane looks is spread over several places. Its surface colour is chosen in `PaneLeaf`, the blue wash for the focused pane is plain CSS, and decorations are separate components. This issue introduces a pane provider, an implementation of what is drawn around a pane and its content, which plugins can register and a theme selects by name.

## What to build

A registry for pane providers, published as a service like the pane registry. A provider draws a panes surface, border, focus marking and any decoration, and is told whether its pane is focused. Grove ships a default provider that draws panes exactly as they look now, including the blue wash. The scrapbook themes use a scrapbook pane provider instead, and its pane carries a sun and a moon. The sun by day or the moon at night travels along the pane when it takes focus and then rests, so showing focus is part of how that pane is drawn and not a separate indicator.

A theme names its provider with an optional field. A theme that names none, or names one that is not registered, gets the default provider, so every existing theme looks the same as today.

## Open questions

Third party plugins run in a sandboxed Worker and cannot hand over a Svelte component. A third party provider probably has to be declarative, in the way the existing declarative surface is, so the first version could ship only core providers.

The landscape painted behind the whole window by the scrapbook themes could belong to this provider or stay a separate window level decoration. Keeping it at the window level is simpler, since one scene has to span every pane and the gaps between them.

The scrapbook themes, the mascot setting and the landscape this builds on are on the branch `marmot-restyle`.

issue:433.title: The theme shown can differ from the theme setting after start
issue:433.author: neoworks-bot
issue:433.body:
When the saved theme in `localStorage` and the `workbench.colorTheme` setting disagree at start, the page shows the first while the store and the Preferences select report the second. This happens when the app is killed before its last `localStorage` write is flushed, and the visible effect is that anything reading the active theme from the store, such as theme specific decorations, does not match what is on screen.

## Cause

The store creates its theme state before `initThemes` applies the saved one, so it always starts as the default theme. At start `applyBaseSettings` then only applies the setting when it differs from the store, so a setting of the default theme is never applied over a different theme that `initThemes` already put on screen.

## Fix

Compare the setting against the theme that is actually applied as well as against the store, and apply it when either differs.

Themes that do not ask for it keep the current sans font. It depends on the issue that adds shape tokens to themes.

issue:429.title: Make the mascot a setting, and let a theme bring its own
issue:429.author: neoworks-bot
issue:429.body:
The marmot now shows in the empty editor and empty agent states, but it is always on and it is the only mascot. This issue adds a "Show the mascot" setting under Appearance and lets a theme supply its own images, so third party themes can have their own avatar.

## What to build

The `Marmot` component becomes a general mascot component that asks the active theme for the image of a named pose, such as "sleeping" or "coder". A theme without a mascot shows nothing, and the setting turns the mascot off for every theme. Catalog themes in `editorCatalog.ts` get an optional field for their mascot images.

## Open question

Whether a theme has to provide every pose or may provide a few, with the rest simply hidden. Hiding is simpler and is what I would start with.

comment.body:
## Evidence

Preferences now has a "Show the Mascot" setting under Appearance, on by default. Turning it off removes the marmot from both the empty editor pane and the agent pane that has no session. Before this change there was no such setting and the marmot was always drawn.

The mascot now comes from the active theme. The four built-in themes carry the marmot, and a catalog theme can bring its own images in an optional `mascot` field, keyed by the poses `empty` and `no-session`. A theme that leaves a pose out simply gets no image there. Catalog images must be `data:` URLs, because the app's content security policy only lets images load from the app itself and from `data:`.

I checked the setting in the app but not a third party theme with its own mascot, because no catalog theme carries one yet. That part is covered by unit tests in `tests/mascot.test.ts`.

issue:428.title: Let a theme set shapes as well as colours, and ship a scrapbook theme
issue:428.author: neoworks-bot
issue:428.body:
Grove themes today only carry a colour palette, but the new Neoworks design system also changes corners, shadows, borders and surfaces. This issue extends the theme registry so a theme can set those shape tokens too, and adds the scrapbook look as one more selectable theme next to the existing ones.

## What to build

A theme gets an optional set of shape tokens: the button, field and popover radii, the raised shadow, and whether surfaces are flat or paper. They are applied to the root element the same way the palette is, and a theme that sets none keeps exactly today values. The scrapbook theme comes in a charcoal and a paper variant, using the forest green brand and warm neutrals from `neoworks.css` in the design system.

## Why a token set

Components must not know which theme is active. They read variables such as `--button-radius`, so the same markup looks sharp in one theme and soft in another, and third party themes from the extensions catalog can set them too.

The first step of this restyle is on the branch `marmot-restyle`.

comment.body:
## Evidence

The theme registry now carries shapes as well as colours, and Preferences lists two new themes, Scrapbook (Dark) and Scrapbook (Light). Before the change the Color Theme select offered only the two Neoworks themes. After it, choosing a scrapbook theme gives warm charcoal or paper surfaces, the forest green primary button, and smaller 3 to 6 pixel corners on panes, buttons and selects.

Switching back to Neoworks (Dark) clears every shape variable from the root element, so the existing themes look exactly as before. The branch is `marmot-restyle`, and `bun test` passes apart from `questionTools.test.ts`, which also fails on `main`.

The first screenshot is the select before the change, the second is Scrapbook (Dark) with the agent pane open, and the third is Scrapbook (Light).

## Out of scope

The shape tokens only affect the radius and shadow scales and the design system Button and Select. Paper surfaces for menus and overlays are tracked in #430.

issue:427.title: Show pull requests and issues on their branches, and replace the GitHub tab with a Launchpad
issue:427.author: neoworks-bot
issue:427.body:
The Git pane's GitHub side nests three levels of tabs: first Repository and GitHub, then pull requests and issues, then list, board and calendar. That is hard to take in at a glance. The plan is to do it the way GitKraken does: pull requests and issues show up where the branches are, and one Launchpad view replaces the GitHub tab.

## In the left column

Pull requests and issues show the same way. A pull request or an issue that has a branch appears on that branch's row. For an issue, the branch is the one Grove names `<issue>-<slug>`. Selecting the row shows the thread in the right panel, where a commit's details go.

Below the branches, a short section lists the pull requests and issues assigned to you that have no branch yet. Each one can start a worktree.

## Launchpad

Launchpad replaces the GitHub tab. It is one list of pull requests and issues, grouped by status, with a pin on each row, in the style of GitKraken's Launchpad.

The search box, the filters and the saved views all stay. The board and the calendar stay as well, as other ways to lay out the same items.

This builds on #425, which merged the git plugins into the one Git pane this changes.

comment.body:
The first step is in. The Git pane's GitHub tab is now Launchpad: one list with the pull requests first, then the issues, each grouped by what it needs. Before this, there were PRs and Issues tabs inside the GitHub tab, with List, Board and Calendar as a third level.

## What it shows

Pull requests are grouped into Needs your review, CI failing, Changes requested, Ready to merge, Waiting on others and Draft. Issues are grouped by who has them. A pin on each row puts the item in a Pinned group at the top, and the item stays in its own group as well. Issues pinned on GitHub show there too.

The search, the filters, the saved views, the board and the calendar all stayed. The search takes `is:pr` and `is:issue` to narrow to one kind, and the board and the calendar lay out the issues among the results.

## How it was checked

In the QA app, a scratch pull request in the sandbox repository showed up under Ready to merge, ahead of the issues. After that I pinned an issue, opened the pull request's thread, narrowed the list to `is:pr`, and switched to the board and the calendar. No errors were logged.

The dashboard query now also fetches who is asked to review each pull request, which is what fills Needs your review. That part is in `src/main`, so Grove needs a restart after the merge.

issue:426.title: e2e teardown fails with kill ESRCH when a straggler exits first
issue:426.author: neoworks-bot
issue:426.body:
An e2e test can fail after all of its checks have passed, with `Error: kill ESRCH` from the fixture's teardown. The teardown first lists the processes that carry the test's profile and then kills them one at a time, so one that exits in between makes `process.kill` throw. Ignoring ESRCH there fixes it, since a process that is already gone is what the teardown wants.

## Where

`killStragglers` in `tests/e2e/fixtures/groveApp.ts` calls `process.kill(pid, 'SIGKILL')` for every pid found under `/proc`, with nothing catching the error.

## Seen

`bun run qa replay 425 --no-build` passed both of its checks and then failed on this, three times in a row on 2026-10-12, after passing cleanly on earlier runs. The timing decides it, so it comes and goes.

issue:425.title: Merge Git, Github and commit graph into a single plugin
issue:425.author: Letsmoe
issue:425.body:
Source Control, the commit graph and the GitHub pane are three separate plugins, and each one reads its own copy of the repository's git state. They drift apart as a result: committing in Source Control leaves the graph showing the old history, because the file watcher ignores `.git` and each view only reloads after its own actions. The fix is to merge them into one `core/git` plugin that owns a single git state every view reads from.

## Shared state

The refs, the branch status, the changed files, the merge state, the stashes and the graph's history move into one store in the plugin. Every git action reloads that store, so whichever view started it, all of them show the result. Today `refs` alone is read separately in three places: the graph, the branches section and the compare section.

## One plugin

The `gitChanges`, `gitGraph` and `github` directories move under `kernel/plugins/git/`, and one plugin registers what the three register today.

## The UI

Everything lives in one center pane called Git, laid out around the commit graph the way GitKraken does it, with a GitHub tab beside it. The Source Control sidebar view goes away, and its rail button and its `<Leader> v g` key open the Git pane instead.

The left column holds the branches, remotes, tags, stashes, checkpoints, commit search and the compare section. The middle is the graph, whose toolbar has the branch with its upstream state and fetch, pull and push. The graph's top row is the working tree. Selecting that row shows the conflicts, the staged and unstaged changes, the commit box and the ship-it or merge bar in the right panel, and selecting a commit shows its details there as before. Everything that used to open Source Control opens the Git pane with the working tree selected.

## Changes from outside

The file watcher ignores `.git`, so a commit or checkout made from a terminal or by an agent reached none of the views either. Each watched worktree also watches its `HEAD` and refs, and the shared state reloads when they move.

comment.body:
Source Control and the commit graph now share one git state, so an action in either one shows in both. Before, a commit made in Source Control never reached the graph. The file watcher ignores `.git`, and each view only reloaded after its own actions.

## What changed

The three plugins are now one, `core/git`, under `kernel/plugins/git/`. Its new `state.svelte.ts` holds the changed files, merge state, branch status, refs and stashes. Every git action reloads it. The views that keep reads of their own, like the commit list, the graph's history and the comparison, read again whenever it reloads. The UI is unchanged so far, and the tabbed Git pane comes next.

## Evidence

The first screenshot is from `main`. The commit "qa: commit from source control" is in Source Control's list, but the graph still starts one commit earlier.

The second is from the branch. A second commit from Source Control shows in the graph at once.

The third shows the other direction. A branch created from a row in the graph is checked out, and Source Control's header, branch list and commit button all follow it.

`tests/e2e/repro/425-merge-git-github-and-commit-graph-into-a.e2e.ts` commits from Source Control and expects the graph to show it. It fails against the code before the fix and passes on the branch. Its teardown fails afterwards with an unrelated `kill ESRCH`, now filed as #426.


![screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neoworks-dev/grove/qa-screenshots/shots/2026-10-12T15-55-49-001-before-graph-stale-after-commit.png)

![screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neoworks-dev/grove/qa-screenshots/shots/2026-10-12T15-55-52-004-after-graph-follows-commit.png)

![screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neoworks-dev/grove/qa-screenshots/shots/2026-10-12T15-55-55-005-after-branch-from-graph-in-source-co.png)

The commit graph and GitHub are now the two tabs of one Git pane, and the git views also follow commits and checkouts made outside Grove. The branch is ready for review.

## The Git pane

The pane has a strip with a Graph tab and a GitHub tab and the window's close button, and each tab keeps its own toolbar under it. Source Control's header has a GitHub button, and its Commits section still has the graph button. The palette has "Show Commit Graph" and "Show GitHub", and an agent opening an issue lands on the GitHub tab. A saved layout that still holds the old Commit Graph or GitHub pane reopens it as the Git pane on the matching tab, which the QA profile showed on restart. The bottom panel's Graph tab is gone.

## Changes from outside Grove

Each watched worktree now also watches its `HEAD`, `MERGE_HEAD` and refs. A commit made with `git commit` in a shell, and then `git checkout -b from-terminal`, both showed in the graph and in Source Control within two seconds. This watch uses `fs.watch` because chokidar reports nothing when git renames a lock file over a ref. It leaves out the index, so a `git add` from a shell alone still waits for the next file change.

## Evidence

The first screenshot shows the Git pane on its Graph tab, the second the GitHub tab opened from Source Control's new button. The third was taken after the commit and checkout from a shell. The fourth shows Source Control's header after the fix described below.

`tests/worktreeWatcher.test.ts` checks that a commit made with git and a branch made in a linked worktree are both reported. `tests/layoutTree.test.ts` checks that the old panes reopen on the right tab. The repro spec passes, apart from the teardown failure in #426.

## Out of scope

Adding the header buttons squeezed the branch name in Source Control down to its first letter, because the "not published" label never shrank. The label now gives way before the name does.

pull:342.title: Share prompt blame through git notes
pull:342.author: neoworks-bot
pull:342.body:
- [x] #338 prompt blame through git notes ([evidence](https://github.com/neoworks-dev/grove/issues/338#issuecomment-5929726666))

Closes #338

Behind a new **Share Prompt Blame** setting (Git, off by default, since it publishes prompt text to the remote). A push notes the commits it publishes under `refs/notes/grove-prompts` and pushes that ref after merging the remote's; a fetch merges the remote's in. Each note holds only the records for the lines its commit added. A notes failure is appended to the push or fetch summary rather than failing the push.

Only Grove's own push (Source Control and a PR's push) annotates. A commit pushed from a terminal gets its note on the next push from Grove, as long as it isn't already on a remote by then.
